page: Microsoft Azure E2s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. This configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local ephemeral storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks reveal a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The E2s_v6 demonstrates strong single-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2149.0 and an average stress-ng single-core CPU performance rating. However, due to its low core count, multi-core performance is limited, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2641.0 and a weak Passmark CPU score of 3745.49. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, showing poor uncached read and write speeds of 21.51 GB/sec and 14.04 GB/sec respectively. Real-world application benchmarks indicate weak performance in database operations and static web serving, alongside a poor Redis SET operations throughput of 2.56 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E2s_v6 offers a low-cost entry point into memory-optimized cloud resources, providing a high memory-to-vCPU density without the expense of larger multi-core instances. This makes it a viable option for lightweight, memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel processing power. Recommended workloads include small-scale databases, caching layers, basic text processing, and lightweight language model inference tasks, such as text generation using small models where it achieves an average speed of 91.22 tokens per second.
